- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.5) — model fails to recognize bearish momentum, leading to persistent overconfidence.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts often stay near recent highs or lows, ignoring true volatility and sentiment-driven corrections.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows lagged reaction to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment drops, underestimating sharp declines.
- When sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.7–0.9), model overweights short-term momentum and fails to adjust for long-term price correction.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends when sentiment is mixed or declining — model overfits to recent highs without accounting for sentiment reversal signals.
